headline: West Haven backs $7.5 million state package for downtown and innovation projects
dek: The announced funding would support public-space and small-business improvements downtown, plus a University of New Haven center focused on workforce training and applied technology.
body: West Haven is set to receive a combined $7.5 million in state-backed support for downtown improvements and a University of New Haven innovation center, state Sen. James Maroney announced Wednesday.

The package includes $2.5 million for public-space work at the West Haven Green and 9 Curtiss Place Plaza and Alleyway. The city says the project also would create a microgrant program for businesses in the Village Improvement District, helping fund leaseholder improvements, vacant-storefront work and facade upgrades.

The remaining $5 million is designated for renovation of the former Railroad Salvage property in Allingtown. The University of New Haven plans to use the site for a Center for Innovation and Applied Technology with workforce-training facilities and space for industry partners.

The projects are part of Connecticut's Community Investment Fund 2030, which directs state bond funding toward community development and economic revitalization. West Haven said the downtown grant's approval by the fund board clears the way for the State Bond Commission to consider final approval, while the university project has been described as a $10 million innovation-center effort supported by a $5 million state grant.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: West Haven gets $7.5 million state funding package
